tokens: READ_AT_RUN: read from verify_at during the run and save the copy with the evidence. WRITE_BEFORE_RUN: the verifier writes the hand verdict into the evidence before the run. HAND_CHECK_AT_RUN: a human judgement from the output plus verify_at. PREVIEW_URL: the PR deploy preview under test, the same value as preview_url in the gate evidence. READ_AT_RUN compares against the response the app itself received (HAR for browser fetches; the app's trace or tool output for server fetches). A separate verifier fetch is allowed only for server-side fetches, within 60 s, with the source timestamp recorded. repeat N: each run id is run N times in a row, unless repeat_by_run overrides it.

input.Your question: Which region had the most earthquakes?

hand_checks.claim: the region the answer names has the most rows in the CSV. Hand rule, independent of the app: region = the text after the last comma of each row's place (the place column; properties.place in the GeoJSON feed), trimmed, or the whole place text when there is no comma (e.g. 'Fiji region'). Only the two-letter codes CA and MX are then translated through PLACE_CODES in app-05-ai-data-analyst/src/lib/liveData/parse.ts:16-19 (CA to California, MX to Mexico), so rows ending in CA and rows ending in California are one region, and the same for MX and Mexico; the app's own output is not used to pick the region If ranks 1 and 2 tie, either name passes.
the earthquake count the answer gives for that region equals the number of CSV rows with that region
the second-ranked region the answer's chart or table shows, and its count, equal the CSV rows with that region If ranks 1 and 2 tie, either name passes.

runs.live_source: https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=40.71&longitude=-74.01&start_date={RUN_DATE:start}&end_date={RUN_DATE:end}&daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum&timezone=auto&format=csv (RUN_DATE = the UTC date the load runs, app-05-ai-data-analyst/src/lib/liveData/load.ts:93; {RUN_DATE:start} and {RUN_DATE:end} come from lastTwelveWholeMonths(RUN_DATE), catalog.ts:90-96; the URL is built by weatherUrl, catalog.ts:98-108)

hand_checks.claim: the month the answer names as highest average max equals the month with the highest mean of temperature_2m_max in this archive CSV If ranks 1 and 2 tie, either name passes.
the average max the answer gives for that month matches the archive CSV mean to one decimal place

the 12 whole months covered are the ones lastTwelveWholeMonths(RUN_DATE) gives in app-05-ai-data-analyst/src/lib/liveData/catalog.ts:90-96: start_date is the 1st of RUN_DATE's UTC month one year earlier, end_date is the last day of the month before RUN_DATE's UTC month, and the request matches the URL saved with the evidence (matches after URL-decoding)

notes: The r3 range is rolling, not frozen: lastTwelveWholeMonths(RUN_DATE) (catalog.ts:90-96) gives a new start_date and end_date on every run. A run must compute them from its own RUN_DATE and save the URL it used with its evidence.
